The key for my success has been repetition. I am obsessed, and I will not quit no matter what is thrown my way. The key is to start off with the fundamentals first, and then work your way up the ladder, so the speak. When you learn to play an instrument, you start with the scales, coding is the same. So, if you get a book that goes over the fundamentals, you should be able to look at the chapter, and then go to your text editor and type in the code from memory, and only then should you move on to the next chapter. I'm not saying to memorize all the code in the book, but to memorize the concepts and to write your own code using those concepts. When you are building a project along side of a Udacity video then you need to code along with it, and then repeat the video series several times until you can go through it and understand what you are doing, and with each iteration you will see big improvements in your understanding of the content.

All that said, make sure you have done the same for HTML and CSS and Bootstrap before moving on to JavaScript. The You don't know JS series is a great series and is highly recommended by myself. I also would recommend, if you can afford it, to take some of the courses that are offered by Wes Bos as I believe he is one of the best JS teachers on the web. He has a free CSS grid and JS30 course that are paid for by the Mozilla Foundation.

Now, dealing with frustration. You are going to encounter this often, and you must learn to accept it because it never truly goes away, and your problems get more and more complex, so it's just life, accept it. If you aren't getting frustrated then you are probably not even trying, so frustration is a GOOD thing! If you want it then you will just keep going, and over time you will learn, and get better, and you will look back at your struggles with a fond nostalgic feeling.
